title: Pseudocode and Simple Flowcharts
learningObjectives: Explain the concept in your own words
Identify the concept in a small example

understand.concept: Pseudocode describes an algorithm in readable, language-neutral steps. A flowchart uses standard shapes and arrows to show sequence, decisions and repetition. Both help plan before writing code.
understand.whyItMatters: These ideas form the foundation for learning every programming language.
understand.history: This lesson focuses on transferable programming concepts; detailed language history is taught in the relevant language module.
understand.analogy: It is like writing clear instructions for a task and following them step by step.
understand.analogyLimit: Programming language rules are precise; a computer does not automatically infer ambiguity in casual human instructions.

explain.narrative: Pseudocode describes an algorithm in readable, language-neutral steps. A flowchart uses standard shapes and arrows to show sequence, decisions and repetition. Both help plan before writing code.

practise.guidedTask: Choose a small everyday task and explain it using the idea of Pseudocode and Simple Flowcharts.
practise.independentTask: Create your own example and explain why each step is needed.
